prompt:
Vertical 9:16 advertising image, full bleed, edge to edge. No border, no device mockup, no frame within the frame.

A man in his late thirties in a plain dark athletic crop top and shorts mid-stride on a wet outdoor running track at dawn, shot from the side during a lateral camera pan. Ordinary, unglamorous, effortful. No gym logos, no branding anywhere.

Documentary sports photography, monochrome. Real athletic effort in a real place. Composition top-weighted: the figure occupies the upper two thirds, the lower third falls into deep unlit shadow and plain surface with no detail. Cinestill 35mm grain and halation. Nothing tack-sharp.

PRODUCT (reproduce EXACTLY as the reference images show; re-light it to this scene, never paste it flat): small injectable glass vial, black rubber cap + gold metal band. Container/source ref: `Dialed Health Injectable.png`
LOCKED: Logo layout is locked (offset diagonal, EKG spike mid-line — see above). Early instruction graphics were REDONE because the model rendered a centered/stacked lockup. Pass `Product Refs/Dialed Health_Logo_Updated-02.png` as a ref whenever DH branding must appear.
LOCKED: Label = logo + product name only. No dosing text, no extra copy — locked since the first vial generation.
LOCKED: Never composite / paste product renders into scenes — always regenerate in-scene with references (house-wide rule; composites read as photoshopped).
LOCKED: Label artwork is sacred in lifestyle shots — it must come EXACTLY from the approved studio shot reference; the model must re-light it to the scene, never invent new text.
LOCKED: Vial upright and vertical in hand-held shots — tilting is what wrecks label fidelity.
LOCKED: Realistic scale — the vial is tiny (~2/3 the length of an index finger); oversized vials were rejected.
LOCKED: Motion blur rule (evolved, current preference): CAMERA-IN-MOTION full-frame blur , not limb-localized. Subtle directional slow-shutter-pan blur permeates the ENTIRE frame (foreground + subject + background); subject is the relative anchor (most legible) but still softer than tack-sharp; background heavily smeared; slight Dutch tilt ~5–8°; shutter feel ~1/30s lateral pan. Say "NOTHING is rigorously tack-sharp" and "the blur is a property of the entire frame, not a single limb." (The older rule — blur must come from a visibly moving limb, never sprinkled on a static pose — still holds as the floor: static-pose sprinkled blur is always wrong.)
PALETTE — STRICTLY MONOCHROMATIC. The only colours permitted anywhere in the frame are this ramp: white #ffffff, gray-50 #f8f8f8, gray-100 #f0f0f0, gray-150 #e8e8e8, gray-200 #dedede, gray-300 #c5c5c5, gray-400 #9a9a9a, gray-500 #6e6e6e, gray-600 #4a4a4a, gray-700 #353535, gray-800 #252525, gray-900 #171717, black #0a0a0a. There is NO accent colour in this brand. No gold, no amber, no warm highlight, no coloured tint of any kind. Any warmth comes from real light on real surfaces, never from a pigment.
